construct: Carotid-sinus and aortic-arch baroreceptors provide rapid buffering of short-term blood-pressure changes. With sustained hypertension, the baroreflex operating point resets toward the chronically elevated pressure and sensitivity may fall, so the reflex does not provide long-term normalization of the elevated pressure.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Arterial baroreceptors buffer acute pressure changes but adapt during sustained hypertension by shifting their pressure-response operating point toward the chronically elevated pressure.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Complete afferent baroreflex failure could reduce corrective reflex output, but it abolishes normal short-term buffering and causes marked blood-pressure lability rather than physiologic resetting in chronic essential hypertension.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Resetting is the only option that preserves baroreceptor function for acute deviations while explaining failure to restore the old chronic pressure.
